regions.0: whole GPU frame: shadow pass, refraction pass, scene pass on all worker lists, postprocess

gather_pcf.equivalence: the same four texels, read by one instruction instead of four and assigned to the same components, so every arithmetic operation downstream is unchanged. Exact if and only if the half-texel-offset address selects the same quad as the four original addresses; that is what the byte-exact oracle tests. The sampler is POINT, so no filtering is being replaced.
gather_pcf.expectation: 6 image_sample down to 3 image instructions in the pixel shader

ablate_ps.equivalence: none: the image is deliberately different. This measures a ceiling, not a candidate.
ablate_ps.expectation: the largest speed-up any change to this shader's body could produce

zeroskip_shadow.pattern_provenance: transferred from phase 2P, not derived from w4's ISA alone; counted separately in the report for that reason
zeroskip_shadow.equivalence: 0 * x == 0 for every finite x, so the result is bit-identical wherever the shadow term is finite. Where it would not be, the images differ and the byte-exact oracle rejects: the rule is not being assumed away.
zeroskip_shadow.expectation: the shadow block skipped on every wave whose lanes are all unlit

abl_lightmath.expectation: removes the length, the reciprocal, the two falloffs and the N.L dot

abl_normalmap.expectation: removes 1 image_sample, 3 rsq and the 3x3 tangent-to-world transform

abl_shadow_taps.expectation: removes 4 image_sample, keeps both 4x4 transforms and the divide

vs_lightspace.predicted_correctness: FAIL tier A and tier B: the shadow depth test is a hard comparison and interpolating the light-space position flips it on boundary pixels
vs_lightspace.equivalence: mathematically identical: the composition of two uniform matrices applied to a position that is itself linearly interpolated. Not bitwise identical, and the difference lands on a hard comparison.
vs_lightspace.expectation: two 4x4 transforms out of the pixel shader, four interpolants in

preregistered_criteria.provenance: every build is gated on the preregistered SHA-256 of every shader the project compiles; the pristine sources are restored on every exit path
preregistered_criteria.correctness: the sample's own render target after a fixed frame count, compared byte for byte against the baseline's. Baseline vs baseline must be identical first or nothing is judged against it
preregistered_criteria.performance: median of the primary timestamp region, several independent processes, counterbalanced order, paired against base
preregistered_criteria.acceptance: median <= -max(1 %, 3 x N95) from this workload's own A/A control, every paired process negative, and correctness passing
